name: De Stijl painting
summary: A picture reduced to straight black lines, rectangles of primary colour and white or grey, in asymmetric balance. Mondrian and van Doesburg wanted a universal language of pure relations that could also order a room or a city.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture shows universal order when it uses only the horizontal and the vertical, the three primaries and the three non-colours, balanced without symmetry.
design_principles: Use only horizontal and vertical lines, with no diagonal and no curve.
Limit colour to red, yellow and blue, plus white, black and grey.
Draw black lines of 1–3% of the picture width, and extend each line to the edge or to another line.
Let white or grey cover 60–75% of the area, so that the colour is rare and strong.
Make each colour field a rectangle, and make no two fields the same size.
Balance the picture asymmetrically: a large red field against several small fields of blue, yellow and grey.
Hold the lines and fields flat and opaque, so that the picture is a plane with no space behind it.
anti_patterns: Diagonal or curved lines, except in the rotated lozenge format
Depth, shadow, texture or visible brush gesture

composition.layout: An orthogonal grid of 4–8 black lines that cross unevenly and divide the canvas into 8–16 rectangles of different sizes; lines run to or past the edge.
composition.focal_point: One large colour field, usually red, at 15–25% of the area, set off-centre in the upper left or lower right quadrant.
composition.format: A square canvas, or a square rotated 45° (the lozenge); a rectangle is allowed at ratios close to 1:1.

principles.rule: Balance the picture asymmetrically: weight of the large red field equals the weight of 3–4 small colour fields and the black line mass.
Divide the canvas in unequal proportions near 1:2, 2:3 or 3:5, and avoid the exact half.
Set white and grey fields at 60–75% of the area as the quiet ground against which colour acts.
Use three levels: one dominant colour field, 2–3 secondary fields, and many white cells.
Spend the primaries at 10–25% of the area in total, in the ratio of about 3 red to 2 blue to 1 yellow.

palette.strategy: Three primaries, three non-colours and nothing else; each colour is pure, flat and opaque, and the white is slightly warm.
palette.distribution: White and pale grey 60–75%, primaries together 10–25%, black lines 5–10%.
palette.ground: A white-primed canvas, painted with an off-white (not pure white) for the ground cells.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint, applied in thin, even layers.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Square, tightly stretched canvas on a plain stretcher.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: No stroke shows; all marks run in one direction in each field, and the painter masks the lines for a sharp edge.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: 2–4 layers of flat, opaque colour; the black lines are laid last or between the fields, with 1–3mm width.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Perfectly hard edges, straight to within 0.5mm.

light_and_modelling.light: No depicted light; the picture itself is bright and even.
light_and_modelling.modelling: None. Each field is a single flat value.
light_and_modelling.shadow: None. A slight difference between two whites or greys is the only tonal step.
light_and_modelling.temperature: Warm red and yellow against cool blue and neutral white, balanced by area.

subject.typical: No subject; a relation of lines and fields. Early studies abstract a tree, a pier or a church tower.
subject.figure_scale: Not applicable: the unit is the field, from 2% to 25% of the area.
subject.treatment: Pure, impersonal and rule-bound; the hand of the artist is hidden.

surface.texture: Smooth, with a faint canvas weave; the paint edge may stand a fraction of a millimetre above the next field.

works.work: Lozenge Composition with Yellow, Black, Blue, Red, and Gray

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). The Farm near Duivendrecht is a pre-De Stijl work and shows the path to abstraction. Counter-Composition VIII is not flagged as public domain by the museum: the id identifies it only. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence; do not copy it.

positive: flat primary red blue yellow fields

emotion.target_response: Clarity and rational calm: the viewer feels a system in balance, with nothing to add or remove.

avoid_when: The brief asks for emotion, a story or a human subject.
The brief needs a soft, organic or ornamental mood.

modifiers.how: Keep the flat colour and the large fields; drop the straight line and the grid, loosen the edges, and make the stroke visible at 50–150mm.
Keep the flat planes and the narrow palette; allow the diagonal and the tilted plane, and bring back an object clue such as a guitar or a bottle.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
Piet Mondrian, Neo-Plasticism: the General Principle of Plastic Equivalence (1920)
